Current milestone M2:
Evidence Import and Signals. Reuse M1 projects. evidence.import(project_id,path) reads an existing bounded local directory or Git working directory without executing source files, following symlinks outside it, or reading .git internals/secrets. It returns {id,project_id,source_path,version,sha256,status,files:[{path,sha256,text}]}; relative paths are stable, digest is SHA-256 of actual content (64 lowercase hex; aggregate algorithm documented). Unchanged refresh keeps the same version identity. evidence.refresh(project_id,evidence_id) rereads the stored path: changed bytes create a new id/version and mark the prior record status=SUPERSEDED. evidence.get(project_id,evidence_id) returns historical/current records. evidence.list(project_id) -> {items:[...]}. signal.create(project_id,evidence_id,text) -> {id,project_id,evidence_id,text,status:OPEN}; signal.reject(project_id,signal_id,reason) persists status=REJECTED and reason; signal.list(project_id) -> {items:[...]}. Reject nonexistent/foreign evidence and blank signal text/rejection reason. Keep historical evidence bytes and source refs.

Current milestone M3:
Claim Ledger. claim.create(project_id,text,evidence_ids) -> {id,project_id,text,evidence_ids,status}; claim.get(project_id,claim_id) recomputes current validity; claim.list(project_id)->{items:[...]}; claim.conflict(project_id,claim_id,reason) marks CONFLICT with persistent reason. A grounded claim whose text is an actual substring of current imported evidence may be SUPPORTED. No evidence or a claim absent from cited evidence is UNSUPPORTED, never silently publishable. Superseded cited evidence yields STALE; explicit conflict yields CONFLICT. This deterministic baseline cannot manufacture inference as fact. Foreign/missing evidence IDs are rejected. Retain all source links and contradiction history. Do not modify prior modules.

Repeating a successful key must not send a second POST. Reusing key with changed revision/payload is rejected. Retry only the specified failed branch; successful siblings untouched. Scheduler. schedule.create(project_id,content_id,platform_url,when,idempotency_key)->{id,status:PENDING,when,...}; when is ISO8601 with timezone offset; reject naive timestamps and unapproved content. schedule.list(project_id)->{items:[...]}; schedule.cancel(project_id,schedule_id)->status CANCELLED; schedule.reschedule(project_id,schedule_id,when) keeps id and appends history; schedule.run_due(project_id,now)->{items:[processed schedule records]}. now is an explicit timezone-aware ISO8601 clock input for reproducible execution; GUI uses current UTC. public_interface.concurrency: Single-threaded assumption per data_dir for this milestone. File system operations should use atomic writes where possible to prevent corruption during simple sequential usage.
public_interface.edge_behavior: The module exposes MILESTONE_ID as 'M1' and a function handle(data_dir, request). It supports operations: project.create(name), project.get(project_id), and project.list(). Data is persisted to disk in data_dir, surviving process restarts. Projects are identified by stable, opaque, non-empty string IDs. Names must be non-empty and preserve Unicode. Two distinct data_dir paths provide complete isolation. Invalid inputs (empty names, missing IDs, unknown ops) raise ValueError. No success-shaped error objects are returned.

ValueError.behavior: Raised when input validation fails (e.g., empty name, missing ID, unsupported op, invalid data_dir type).

idempotency.handle: Non-idempotent for create; idempotent for get and list.

handle.behavior: Dispatches based on request['op']. Validates input types and constraints. Interacts with the underlying storage layer to perform create, get, or list actions. Ensures persistence across calls.

handle.ordering: Sequential execution within a single call; no concurrent internal locking required for basic correctness if external serialization is assumed, but file-level atomicity is preferred.

handle.returns: dict (JSON-compatible result specific to the operation)

public_interface.concurrency: Single-threaded assumption per data_dir for this milestone. File system operations should use atomic writes where possible to prevent corruption during simple sequential usage.
public_interface.edge_behavior: The module exposes MILESTONE_ID as 'M1' and a function handle(data_dir, request). It supports operations: project.create(name), project.get(project_id), and project.list(). Data is persisted to disk in data_dir, surviving process restarts. Projects are identified by stable, opaque, non-empty string IDs. Names must be non-empty and preserve Unicode. Two distinct data_dir paths provide complete isolation. Invalid inputs (empty names, missing IDs, unknown ops) raise ValueError. No success-shaped error objects are returned.

ValueError.behavior: Raised when input validation fails (e.g., empty name, missing ID, unsupported op, invalid data_dir type).

idempotency.handle: Non-idempotent for create; idempotent for get and list.

handle.behavior: Dispatches based on request['op']. Validates input types and constraints. Interacts with the underlying storage layer to perform create, get, or list actions. Ensures persistence across calls.
handle.idempotency: Non-idempotent for create; idempotent for get and list.
handle.name: handle
handle.ordering: Sequential execution within a single call; no concurrent internal locking required for basic correctness if external serialization is assumed, but file-level atomicity is preferred.
handle.parameters: data_dir: str (filesystem path), request: dict (JSON-compatible with 'op' key)
handle.returns: dict (JSON-compatible result specific to the operation)

ordering.handle: Sequential execution within a single call; no concurrent internal locking required for basic correctness if external serialization is assumed, but file-level atomicity is preferred.

public_interface.persistence: Filesystem-based storage within the provided data_dir. Format is agent-owned (e.g., JSON files or SQLite) but must ensure durability across separate Python processes. Isolation between different data_dir paths is strict.

public_interface.concurrency: Single-threaded assumption per data_dir for this milestone. File system operations should use atomic writes where possible to prevent corruption during simple sequential usage.
public_interface.edge_behavior:
The module exposes MILESTONE_ID as 'M2' and handle(data_dir, request). It supports operations: evidence.import(project_id, path), evidence.refresh(project_id, evidence_id), evidence.get(project_id, evidence_id), evidence.list(project_id), signal.create(project_id, evidence_id, text), signal.reject(project_id, signal_id, reason), signal.list(project_id). 

evidence.import reads a bounded local directory or Git working directory without executing source files, following symlinks outside it, or reading .git internals/secrets. Returns {id, project_id, source_path, version, sha256, status, files:[{path, sha256, text}]}. Relative paths are stable. Digest is SHA-256 of actual content (64 lowercase hex). Unchanged refresh keeps same version identity.

evidence.refresh rereads stored path: changed bytes create new id/version and mark prior record status=SUPERSEDED.

evidence.get returns historical/current records.

evidence.list returns {items:[...]}. 

signal.create returns {id, project_id, evidence_id, text, status:OPEN}. Rejects nonexistent/foreign evidence and blank text.
signal.reject persists status=REJECTED and reason. Rejects blank reason.
signal.list returns {items:[...]}.

Invalid input, unknown IDs, cross-project access, unsupported operations raise ValueError. No success-shaped error objects. Persistence survives process restarts.

ValueError.behavior: Raised when input validation fails (e.g., empty name, missing ID, unsupported op, invalid data_dir type, non-existent project/evidence/signal, foreign evidence reference, blank text/reason, path traversal/security violation).

public_interface.edge_behavior:
The module exposes MILESTONE_ID as 'M3' and handle(data_dir, request). It supports operations: claim.create(project_id, text, evidence_ids), claim.get(project_id, claim_id), claim.list(project_id), claim.conflict(project_id, claim_id, reason).

claim.create validates that the project exists and all provided evidence_ids exist within that project. If any evidence_id is missing or belongs to a different project, raise ValueError. The initial status is computed deterministically:
- SUPPORTED: If the claim text is an exact substring of the current (non-SUPERSEDED) text content of at least one cited evidence file.
- UNSUPPORTED: If no evidence is cited, or if the claim text is not found in any current cited evidence.
- STALE: If all cited evidence records are SUPERSEDED.
- CONFLICT: Only set via explicit conflict operation; create never sets this initially unless logic dictates otherwise (but spec says 'explicit conflict yields CONFLICT', implying create starts as SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED/STALE).
Returns {id, project_id, text, evidence_ids, status}.

claim.get recomputes the current validity status based on the latest state of the cited evidence (checking for supersession or new support) and returns the updated record. Returns {id, project_id, text, evidence_ids, status}.

claim.list returns {items: [...]} containing all claims for the project with their currently computed statuses.

claim.conflict marks a specific claim as CONFLICT with a persistent reason. This overrides the computed status until the claim is potentially re-evaluated or modified (though modification isn't supported here, so it stays CONFLICT). Raises ValueError if claim_id doesn't exist or belongs to another project.

claim.conflict marks a specific claim as CONFLICT with a persistent reason. claim.create validates that the project exists and all provided evidence_ids exist within that project. If any evidence_id is missing or belongs to a different project, raise ValueError. The initial status is computed deterministically:
- SUPPORTED: If the claim text is an exact substring of the current (non-SUPERSEDED) text content of at least one cited evidence file.
- UNSUPPORTED: If no evidence is cited, or if the claim text is not found in any current cited evidence.
- STALE: If all cited evidence records are SUPERSEDED.
- CONFLICT: Only set via explicit conflict operation; create never sets this initially unless logic dictates otherwise (but spec says 'explicit conflict yields CONFLICT', implying create starts as SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED/STALE).
Returns {id, project_id, text, evidence_ids, status}.

claim.get recomputes the current validity status based on the latest state of the cited evidence (checking for supersession or new support) and returns the updated record. Returns {id, project_id, text, evidence_ids, status}.

claim.list returns {items: [...]} containing all claims for the project with their currently computed statuses.

claim.conflict marks a specific claim as CONFLICT with a persistent reason. This overrides the computed status until the claim is potentially re-evaluated or modified (though modification isn't supported here, so it stays CONFLICT). Raises ValueError if claim_id doesn't exist or belongs to another project.

It supports operations: campaign.create(project_id, name, audience, channels), campaign.get(project_id, campaign_id), campaign.update(project_id, campaign_id, name, audience, channels), campaign.archive(project_id, campaign_id), campaign.list(project_id).

campaign.create validates that the project exists. Rejects blank/whitespace-only name or audience. Rejects empty channels list. Rejects non-string elements in channels. Ensures channels are unique. Returns {id, project_id, name, audience, channels, status: 'ACTIVE', history: [...]}.

campaign.get retrieves a campaign by ID within the specified project. Raises ValueError if not found or belongs to another project.

campaign.update modifies name, audience, and channels for an existing ACTIVE campaign. Preserves the original ID. Appends the previous state to the history array. Validates inputs similarly to create. Raises ValueError if campaign not found, belongs to another project, or is ARCHIVED.

campaign.archive sets the status of an existing campaign to 'ARCHIVED'. Raises ValueError if campaign not found or belongs to another project.

campaign.list returns {items: [...]} containing all campaigns for the given project.

Invalid input, unknown IDs, cross-project access, and unsupported operations raise ValueError. No success-shaped error objects. Persistence survives process restarts.

policy.behavior: Raised when input validation fails (e.g., empty name/audience, empty/non-unique/non-string channels, missing/invalid project/campaign IDs, foreign campaign reference, archived campaign update attempt, unsupported op).

public_interface.edge_behavior:
The source module publish_publish.py exposes MILESTONE_ID as 'M7' and handle(data_dir, request). It supports operations: publish.send(project_id, content_id, platform_url, idempotency_key), publish.get(project_id, receipt_id), publish.list(project_id), publish.reconcile(project_id, receipt_id, platform_url), publish.retry(project_id, receipt_id, platform_url).

publish.send consults M6 approval status and current claims/media before sending. It performs a POST to platform_url+'/publish' with JSON {idempotency_key, project_id, content_id, revision, channel, text}. A 200 response yields PUBLISHED status with remote_id and url. An HTTP 429 yields RATE_LIMITED. Timeout or connection loss after request initiation yields UNKNOWN (no blind retry). Repeating a successful key must not send a second POST. Reusing a key with changed revision/payload is rejected.

publish.reconcile performs a GET to '/publications?key='+URL-encoded key. A 200 response confirms PUBLISHED; a 404 proves absent and records that fact before retry can issue POST.

publish.retry only retries the specified failed branch; successful siblings are untouched.

Receipts include id, project_id, content_id, revision, channel, status (PUBLISHED, RATE_LIMITED, UNKNOWN, FAILED), remote_id (null until known), idempotency_key, request_ref, response_ref, attempts:[{operation,status,started_at,ended_at}], url.

Different contents/channels can publish concurrently with safe persistent receipts and real interval overlap.

serve_platform(host, port, data_dir) provides a real local threaded HTTP test platform with persistent idempotent /publish, /publications, and /metrics?remote_id= routes, no upstream publishing.

early_main.py provides a usable browser GUI. It starts with python early_main.py --serve --port PORT --data DIR; no args shows help and exits 0. GET /health returns JSON {status:'ok'}. The GUI communicates with the backend through POST /api/action {milestone:'M1'..'M7',...op request} and JSON response. It implements the workflow: Projects -> Campaign -> Content -> Review/Approve -> Local Publish -> Receipt. Forms expose accessible labels Project name, Campaign name, Audience, Channels (comma-separated text), Content text (textarea), Channel (select with actual campaign channels), Claims (select displaying current claim text), Platform URL. Buttons Create project, Create campaign, Save content, Review, Approve, Publish. With one project/campaign, selection may default to that real object. Successful creation shows the actual name; receipts visibly show remote IDs. Errors use role=alert and progress/result messages use role=status. A reload keeps selected persisted project data. Never proxy a static fake screen.

early_main.py provides a usable browser GUI. It starts with python early_main.py --serve --port PORT --data DIR; no args shows help and exits 0. GET /health returns JSON {status:'ok'}. The GUI communicates with the backend through POST /api/action {milestone:'M1'..'M7',...op request} and JSON response. It implements the workflow: Projects -> Campaign -> Content -> Review/Approve -> Local Publish -> Receipt. Forms expose accessible labels Project name, Campaign name, Audience, Channels (comma-separated text), Content text (textarea), Channel (select with actual campaign channels), Claims (select displaying current claim text), Platform URL. Buttons Create project, Create campaign, Save content, Review, Approve, Publish. With one project/campaign, selection may default to that real object. Successful creation shows the actual name; receipts visibly show remote IDs. Errors use role=alert and progress/result messages use role=status. A reload keeps selected persisted project data. Never proxy a static fake screen.
